description: 1. The agent must locate `audit.py` in the workspace root — the only supply-chain risk tool available — and read its usage signature from the SKILL.md (`python audit.py path/to/skill.md > report.md`). 2. The agent must identify `vendor_intake/flagged/vendor-data-sync.skill.md` as the target (the only file in the flagged directory), NOT any of the distractor approved/archived skills. 3. The agent must invoke `python audit.py vendor_intake/flagged/vendor-data-sync.skill.md > vendor_risk_report.md` (or equivalent shell redirection), correctly capturing stdout into the markdown file. 4. The tool's heuristics will detect ≥3 patterns in the flagged file (HTTP POST exfiltration, ~/.env reads, credential keywords, curl to unknown domain), causing the risk level to be rated HIGH. 5. The resulting `vendor_risk_report.md` must contain the canonical audit.py output structure: `# Security Audit Report`, `## Risk Level: HIGH`, `## Findings` listing the detected patterns, `## Permission Manifest` with categorized touches, and `## Summary` reporting the count. An agent that tries to write its own scanner or produce a generic markdown file without using audit.py will fail the structural and content checks.
